rubric_items.reason: Each of the six ticket acceptance criteria maps to a REQ (AC1-REQ-1, AC2-REQ-2/3/4, AC3-REQ-5, AC4-REQ-6/7, AC5-REQ-8, AC6-REQ-9). Out-of-scope items give reasons.
Each REQ covers one behaviour a tester can check. One flaw: the REQ-5 YAML statement misplaces its backticks, so the exact notice text a tester would assert on is unclear.
Every REQ cites a ticket line or an IDE answer. REQ-3 and REQ-4 rest on A-01 and A-02. The only assumption (REQ-6) was confirmed in A-04. No invented values.
The divergence from AC2 caused by dropping the 50-cap is recorded as a mismatch on A-02 and cites ticket L28-L30. No baseline conflict was left silent.
Questions are precise, offer real options and propose defaults. The override of AC2 was decided by an engineer, but it is arguably a product decision.
Plain wording and consistent glossary terms. Small glitches: a malformed quote in REQ-5, a stray `Yes, confirm` in REQ-6, and a non-scope bullet listed under Out of scope.
